q1.question: O Compass pode dizer-me que país escolher?
q1.answer: Não. A ferramenta analisa sistemas e simula cenários, mas a decisão final é tua. Fornecemos informação, tu fazes as tuas próprias escolhas.

q2.question: Os dados são fiáveis?
q2.answer: Usamos fontes públicas (índices de corrupção, dados fiscais, rankings de passaportes). Estes dados são indicativos e podem mudar. Verifica sempre com fontes oficiais antes de tomar decisões importantes.

q3.question: Qual é a diferença entre "A minha simulação" e "Modo educativo"?
q3.answer: "A minha simulação" (Chaves de Saída) analisa a TUA situação real com os TEUS parâmetros. O "Modo educativo" faz-te interpretar um personagem FICTÍCIO aleatório para entender mecanismos sem envolvimento pessoal.

q4.question: É grátis?
q4.answer: Sim, a ferramenta é gratuita. Podes criar uma conta para sincronizar os teus dados entre dispositivos, mas não é obrigatório.

q5.question: Os meus dados pessoais estão protegidos?
q5.answer: Os dados de simulação ficam no teu dispositivo ou na tua conta pessoal. Não vendemos os teus dados nem os partilhamos com ninguém.

q6.question: Posso usar esta ferramenta para decisões importantes?
q6.answer: Esta ferramenta é um ponto de partida para a tua reflexão, não uma fonte de verdade absoluta. Para decisões importantes (imigração, impostos, saúde), consulta sempre profissionais qualificados.

jsonld.a1: Compass est la première plateforme d'aide à la décision pour la relocalisation internationale. Elle analyse 80+ país en profondeur : fiscalité, coût de la vie, visas, qualité de vie et profils compatibles.
jsonld.q2: How does the expat profile test work?
jsonld.a2: Le test rapide évalue vos priorités (fiscalité, qualité de vie, sécurité, opportunités) en 2 minutes. Il vous suggère les país les plus compatibles avec votre profil spécifique, contrairement aux classements génériques.
jsonld.a3: L'accès de base est gratuit : test rapide, exploration des 80+ país, comparaison basique. Le plan Premium à 9,90€/mois donne accès aux stratégies de sortie, simulateur fiscal et analyses approfondies.
jsonld.q4: Where does Compass data come from?
jsonld.a4: Data comes from the World Bank, OECD, IMF, Transparency International, Numbeo and government sources. Intelligence is updated regularly via verified sources.
jsonld.q5: Puis-je comparer plusieurs país pour mon expatriation ?
jsonld.a5: Sim, l'outil de comparaison permet de comparer jusqu'à 4 país simultanément sur fiscalité, coût de la vie, qualité de vie, visas, sécurité et plus, avec des radar charts et exports PDF.
jsonld.q6: How is Compass different from classic expatriation guides?
jsonld.a6: Compass analyse chaque país en profondeur, identifie les profils qui réussissent ou peinent dans chaque contexte, et propose des stratégies personnalisées plutôt que des classements génériques.
jsonld.q7: Quels país sont couverts par Compass ?
jsonld.a7: Compass couvre 80+ país : Europe (France, Suisse, Portugal, Allemagne...), Amérique (USA, Canada, Mexique...), Asie (Thaïlande, Japon, Singapour...), Médio-Orient (Émirats, Qatar...) et Afrique.
jsonld.q8: How does the tax simulator work?
jsonld.a8: Le simulateur fiscal calcule votre impôt sur le revenu dans le país de destination et le compare à votre situation actuelle. Il intègre les régimes spéciaux, conventions de double imposition et optimisations légales.

keyConcept.title: Conceito chave: Tendência ≠ Certeza
keyConcept.explanation: Quando a ferramenta diz 'este sistema tende a favorecer X', significa que estatisticamente, neste tipo de contexto, X é mais provável. Mas o TEU caso particular depende de milhares de fatores que a ferramenta não conhece.
keyConcept.analogy: É como o tempo: 'Chove frequentemente em novembro em Paris' é estatisticamente verdade, mas não prevê se choverá a 15 de novembro quando TU lá estiveres.

systemError.name: Erro de sistema
systemError.shortDescription: Ignorar as regras reais do sistema em que operas.
systemError.definition: Agir de acordo com expectativas pessoais em vez das regras reais do sistema (fiscal, legal, social) a que estás sujeito.
systemError.whyItHappens: Frequentemente projetamos regras do nosso país de origem ou ambiente familiar num novo contexto. Informação fiável é difícil de encontrar e os sistemas são complexos.
systemError.timeCost: 6 meses a 2 anos de procedimentos ou adaptação

metricError.name: Erro de métrica
metricError.shortDescription: Otimizar o indicador errado ou medir apenas o que tranquiliza.
metricError.definition: Focar em indicadores superficiais (salário bruto, prestígio) ignorando métricas que realmente importam (qualidade de vida, custo real, progresso).
metricError.whyItHappens: Métricas visíveis são fáceis de comunicar e comparar. Métricas importantes são frequentemente invisíveis ou desconfortáveis de medir.
metricError.timeCost: Anos a perseguir o objetivo errado
metricError.moneyCost: Investimentos em áreas que não trazem nada

timingError.name: Erro de timing
timingError.shortDescription: Agir cedo demais, tarde demais, ou ignorar os ciclos do sistema.
timingError.definition: Não ter em conta os ciclos económicos, sazonais ou institucionais que determinam o sucesso de uma ação.
timingError.whyItHappens: A impaciência empurra para ação imediata. Ciclos longos são difíceis de perceber quando estás dentro deles.
timingError.energyCost: Frustração de nadar contra a corrente

irreversibilityError.name: Erro de irreversibilidade
irreversibilityError.shortDescription: Comprometer-se com uma decisão difícil de corrigir sem testá-la.
irreversibilityError.definition: Tomar uma decisão de alto compromisso (casamento, compra de imóvel, expatriação permanente) sem fase de teste ou possibilidade de retirada.
irreversibilityError.whyItHappens: A pressão social valoriza o compromisso total. Testar antes de se comprometer é por vezes visto como falta de confiança.
irreversibilityError.timeCost: Anos a corrigir um erro ou a viver com ele
irreversibilityError.moneyCost: Custos de saída muito altos (divórcio, venda com prejuízo)

hiddenCostError.name: Erro de custo oculto
hiddenCostError.shortDescription: Subestimar os custos reais para além do preço visível.
hiddenCostError.definition: Ver apenas custos visíveis (preço, salário) ignorando custos ocultos (manutenção, stress, tempo, oportunidades perdidas).
hiddenCostError.whyItHappens: Vendedores e sistemas minimizam custos ocultos. O nosso cérebro prefere números simples a cálculos complexos.
hiddenCostError.timeCost: Horas invisíveis de manutenção e gestão

egoError.name: Erro de ego
egoError.shortDescription: Deixar o estatuto ou imagem guiar decisões económicas.
egoError.definition: Tomar decisões baseadas no que queres projetar em vez do que realmente precisas.
egoError.whyItHappens: O estatuto social é uma necessidade humana fundamental. A perceção dos outros influencia as nossas escolhas mais do que admitimos.
egoError.timeCost: Energia gasta a manter uma imagem
egoError.moneyCost: Compras de estatuto à custa da segurança
egoError.energyCost: Ansiedade relacionada com manter as aparências

environmentError.name: Erro de ambiente
environmentError.shortDescription: Ignorar a influência do ambiente nos teus resultados.
environmentError.definition: Acreditar que o sucesso depende apenas do esforço pessoal ignorando o papel do contexto (país, rede, época, setor).
environmentError.whyItHappens: A meritocracia é uma narrativa dominante. Reconhecer o papel do ambiente pode parecer diminuir os próprios méritos.
environmentError.timeCost: Anos a estagnar no ambiente errado
environmentError.moneyCost: Potencial não realizado por mau posicionamento

narrativeError.name: Erro de narrativa
narrativeError.shortDescription: Confundir uma história inspiradora com uma estratégia aplicável.
narrativeError.definition: Seguir uma narrativa (história de sucesso, conselho de guru) sem verificar se se aplica à tua própria situação.
narrativeError.whyItHappens: Histórias são mais memoráveis que estatísticas. O viés do sobrevivente torna os sucessos mais visíveis que os fracassos.
narrativeError.timeCost: Anos a seguir um roteiro inadequado
narrativeError.moneyCost: Investimentos em formação ou conselhos irrelevantes
narrativeError.energyCost: Dúvidas sobre si mesmo quando os resultados prometidos não chegam

sunkCost.name: Custo afundado
sunkCost.shortDescription: Continuar a investir porque já investiste demais.
sunkCost.definition: Prosseguir uma ação desfavorável porque já comprometeste tempo, dinheiro ou energia que não queres perder.
sunkCost.whyItHappens: O nosso cérebro odeia perdas. Admitir um erro passado é doloroso. Esperamos que a situação melhore.
sunkCost.timeCost: Anos adicionais num beco sem saída
sunkCost.moneyCost: Investimentos adicionais para justificar os anteriores
sunkCost.energyCost: Exaustão a manter algo que não funciona

socialProofError.name: Erro de prova social
socialProofError.shortDescription: Imitar outros sem verificar se a situação deles se aplica à tua.
socialProofError.definition: Seguir o comportamento da maioria ou de figuras admiradas sem analisar se as suas restrições e objetivos são os mesmos.
socialProofError.whyItHappens: Seguir o grupo reduz a incerteza. Se os outros fazem assim, deve ser o método correto.
socialProofError.timeCost: Anos a seguir um caminho que não é o teu
socialProofError.energyCost: Fosso entre aspirações e vida diária

concept.title: The Concept
concept.description: PYRAMIDES est un jeu de stratégie où tu gères des trajectoires de vie. Tu ne choisis pas ton point de départ : tu tires des personnages avec un país de naissance, des traits, et des aspirations. À chaque 'année' de jeu, tu prends des décisions : travailler, étudier, soigner, migrer, entreprendre, construire ton réseau, nourrir tes relations... Le monde bouge, les país ont leurs règles, et la réussite dépend de ta capacité à optimiser sous contrainte.

welcome.title: Bienvenue dans le Qui de la Vie
welcome.content: This game simulates the realities that millions of people experience around the world. This is not fiction — it's a mirror of the real world, with its opportunities and dangers.
welcome.reality: Every mechanic in this game reflects a lived reality. Our goal is prevention and understanding, not fear.

lifeAssignment.title: You don't choose your starting life
lifeAssignment.content: Like in real life, you don't choose where you're born, your starting economic situation, or your initial constraints. The game assigns you a random life — some easier, some very difficult.
lifeAssignment.reality: Naître dans un país stable avec un bon passeport est un privilège. D'autres doivent lutter pour des droits que beaucoup considèrent acquis.
examples: Un Suisse né à Genève vs un Nigérian né à Lagos — mêmes ambitions, opportunités très différentes
Une femme née en Arabie Saoudite vs une née au Canada — libertés fondamentales différentes
Un enfant né dans une famille riche vs une famille pauvre — même país, trajectoires différentes

resources.title: Your life resources
resources.content: You manage 6 essential resources: Health, Money, Network, Security, Education and Morale. Every decision affects them. If some drop to zero, consequences can be severe.
resources.reality: In real life, losing your health or network can mean the end of all opportunities. Money alone doesn't protect from everything.
examples: Santé : une maladie chronique change tout le calcul de l'expatriation
Réseau : sans contacts, même les compétences ne suffisent pas
Sécurité : un passeport faible limite drastiquement les options

pyramids.title: Chaque país a son système
pyramids.content: Les 6 types de pyramides représentent comment chaque país fonctionne vraiment. Certains récompensent la compétence, d'autres les connexions, d'autres encore l'extraction de ressources.
pyramids.reality: Comprendre le système d'un país est crucial. Ce qui fonctionne en Allemagne peut être fatal au Cameroun, et vice versa.

events.title: Life sends you events
events.content: Each turn, global and local events affect your resources. Economic crises, opportunities, natural disasters, political changes — you must adapt.
events.reality: Nobody controls everything. Migrants who planned everything can see their plans destroyed by a policy change overnight.
examples: Une crise économique mondiale peut effacer des années d'épargne
Un nouveau gouvernement peut fermer les frontières ou changer les règles du visa

actions.title: Your choices define your trajectory
actions.content: Each turn, you can work, study, network, save, or take risks. Major actions have more impact but carry more risk.
actions.reality: Every choice has an opportunity cost. Studying means less immediate money. Working hard without a network may lead nowhere.

shortcuts.title: Dangerous shortcuts
shortcuts.content: The game offers 'shortcuts' — illegal crossing, undocumented work, fake documents. These options exist because they exist in real life. Consequences can be catastrophic.
shortcuts.reality: Every year, thousands of people die attempting these shortcuts. In Libya, human trafficking is a reality. This game doesn't glorify these choices — it shows their real consequences.
examples: Traversée de la Méditerranée : risque réel de mort, interception, ou esclavage
Faux documents : emprisonnement, déportation, interdiction de retour
Travail au noir : exploitation, absence de protection, vulnérabilité totale

aspirations.title: Your personal goals
aspirations.content: Your character has aspirations — becoming wealthy, living safely, reuniting with family, or simply surviving. Success is measured against YOUR goals, not a universal standard.
aspirations.reality: 'Success' is relative. A refugee who rebuilds their life has accomplished as much as an entrepreneur who becomes a millionaire.

endgame.title: Life summary
endgame.content: At the end, the game evaluates whether you achieved your aspirations, preserved your health, and navigated the system. There's no 'right' way to play — only choices and their consequences.
endgame.reality: This game is a tool for understanding. Whether it helps you appreciate your situation or better understand others', that's its real victory.

bias.title: Cognitive Biases
bias.subtitle: The invisible filters of our decisions

s1.title: Introdução
s1.p1: Our brain is an extraordinary machine, capable of processing millions of pieces of information per second. To achieve this, it uses shortcuts — heuristics that allow us to decide quickly.
s1.p2: Ces raccourcis sont précieux dans la vie quotidienne. Maios ils peuvent devenir des pièges dans les décisions importantes, là où la nuance compte.

s2.title: The most common biases
s2.i1: Confirmation bias: seeking information that confirms what we already believe
s2.i2: Anchoring bias: giving too much importance to the first information received
s2.i3: Availability bias: overestimating what is easily memorable
s2.i4: Survivorship bias: seeing only successes, not silent failures
s2.i5: Status quo bias: preferring not to change, even when suboptimal
s2.i6: Loss aversion: fearing loss more than desiring gain

s3.title: Why it's hard to see
s3.p1: Biases are invisible precisely because they are part of how we think. We can't 'step out' of our brain to observe it from outside.
s3.p2: That's why thinking frameworks, reading grids, and dialogue with other perspectives are so important. They create distance — a space to see what escapes us.

bias.quote: The first step toward clarity is not eliminating biases — it's admitting we have them.

s4.title: What to do?
s4.p1: It's not about eliminating biases — that's impossible. It's about creating conditions where they have less grip on important decisions.
s4.p2: Slow down. Write. Question certainties. Seek divergent opinions. Distinguish what we know from what we assume.

bias.key1: Biases are useful shortcuts — except in complex decisions
bias.key2: We can't eliminate them, but we can create distance
bias.key3: Methodical doubt is a tool, not a weakness

irreversible.title: Irreversible Decisions
irreversible.subtitle: Distinguishing what can be undone from what cannot

s1.title: The uniformity trap
s1.p1: We tend to treat all decisions the same way. Yet some can be cancelled with a few clicks; others commit for years, or forever.
s1.p2: Confusing the two means either hesitating too long on what doesn't matter, or committing too fast on what does.

s2.title: A simple typology
s2.i1: Tipo 1 : Irréversibles. Une fois franchies, pas de retour. Exemples : avoir un enfant, révéler un secret, détruire une relation.
s2.i2: Tipo 2 : Réversibles avec coût. On peut revenir en arrière, mais ça coûte (temps, argent, énergie). Exemples : changer de país, quitter un emploi, acheter un bien.
s2.i3: Tipo 3 : Facilement réversibles. Peu de conséquences à annuler. Exemples : tester un outil, modifier un document, reporter une réunion.

irreversible.warning: Atenção : nous sous-estimons souvent le coût de réversibilité. "Je pourrai toujours revenir" est parfois une illusion confortable.

s3.title: Adapting your method
s3.p1: Maios une décision est irréversible, plus elle mérite du temps, de la réflexion et des perspectives multiples.
s3.p2: Les décisions de Tipo 1 demandent une vraie pause. Pas de l'hésitation stérile — mais du temps pour voir ce qu'on ne voit pas encore.

irreversible.key1: Tudoes les décisions ne méritent pas le même investissement
irreversible.key2: The cost of reversibility is often underestimated
irreversible.key3: Maios c'est irréversible, plus ça mérite du temps

control.title: Illusion of Control
control.subtitle: What really depends on us

s1.title: The myth of "anything is possible"
s1.p1: Contemporary culture values agency: "if you want it, you can do it". Sometimes true. Sometimes a cruel lie.
s1.p2: We evolve in systems — economic, social, institutional — that constrain our possibilities. Ignoring them is preparing for disappointment.

s2.title: Three zones to distinguish
s2.i1: Control zone: what depends entirely on me (my actions, my reactions, my effort)
s2.i2: Influence zone: what I can act on, but without guarantee (my relationships, certain opportunities)
s2.i3: Acceptance zone: what escapes me (the market, others' decisions, chance)

s3.title: Why it matters
s3.p1: Confusing these zones generates either frustration (when we fail to control the uncontrollable), or passivity (when we give up acting where we can).
s3.p2: Clarity consists of investing energy where it has grip, and accepting the rest — not by resignation, but by realism.

control.key1: Tudo n'est pas sous notre contrôle — et c'est normal
control.key2: Distinguishing control, influence, and acceptance saves energy

speed.title: Speed vs Haste
speed.subtitle: Acting fast is not acting in urgency

s1.title: Two ways to go fast
s1.p1: Speed can be a strategic advantage. Acting before others, seizing an opportunity, iterating quickly — all this has value.
s1.p2: Maios il y a une différence entre la vitesse délibérée et la précipitation. L'une est choisie ; l'autre est subie.

s2.title: Signs of haste
s2.i1: No time to ask "is this really urgent?"
s2.i2: Ignoring doubts because we must move forward
s2.i3: Justifying haste by fear of missing out
s2.i4: Unable to clearly explain why now

s3.title: The real question
s3.p1: Before acting fast, ask yourself: "Am I choosing this speed, or am I suffering it?"
s3.p2: Chosen speed is powerful. Suffered haste is dangerous.

speed.key1: Speed can be an asset — if chosen
speed.key2: Haste is often a symptom, not a strategy
speed.key3: Taking 5 minutes to ask the question can avoid 5 months of regret

individual.title: Individual vs System
individual.subtitle: Personal responsibility and structural constraints

s1.title: A false dilemma
s1.p1: On one side, the "anything is possible if you believe" discourse. On the other, systemic fatalism: "the system is against you".
s1.p2: Both are true — and false. Reality is more nuanced: we act in systems that constrain us AND offer possibilities.

s2.title: What the system does
s2.p1: A system defines rules, incentives, obstacles. It rewards certain behaviors and punishes others. It creates easy paths and dead ends.
s2.p2: Ignoring the system means fighting invisible forces. Understanding it means knowing where to place your efforts.

s3.title: What remains for the individual
s3.p1: Even in the most constraining systems, margins remain. Choices. Ways to navigate.
s3.p2: Individual responsibility is not about controlling everything — it's about doing the maximum with what is under our control.

individual.key2: Understanding the system helps navigate it better
individual.key3: Responsibility applies to what depends on us, not the rest

jsonld.a1: Compass is a country comparison platform for international relocation. It analyzes 80+ countries: taxation, visas, cost of living, compatible profiles, unwritten rules.
jsonld.q2: How does the expat profile test work?
jsonld.a2: The quick test evaluates your priorities (taxation, quality of life, safety, opportunities) in 2 minutes. It suggests the countries most compatible with your specific profile, unlike generic rankings.
jsonld.a3: Basic access is free: quick test, exploration of 80+ countries, basic comparison. The Premium plan at €9.90/month gives access to strategies, fiscal simulator and detailed analyses.
jsonld.q4: Where does Compass data come from?
jsonld.a4: Data comes from the World Bank, OECD, IMF, Transparency International, Numbeo and government sources. Intelligence is updated regularly via verified sources.
jsonld.q5: Can I compare multiple countries for my expatriation?
jsonld.a5: Yes, the comparison tool allows you to compare up to 4 countries simultaneously on taxation, cost of living, quality of life, visas, safety and more, with radar charts and PDF exports.
jsonld.q6: How is Compass different from classic expatriation guides?
jsonld.a6: Compass analyzes each country in depth (who succeeds, who struggles, unwritten rules) and offers personalized strategies rather than generic rankings.
jsonld.q7: Which countries are covered by Compass?
jsonld.a7: Compass covers 80+ countries: Europe (France, Switzerland, Portugal, Germany...), Americas (USA, Canada, Mexico...), Asia (Thailand, Japan, Singapore...), Middle East (UAE, Qatar...) and Africa.
jsonld.q8: How does the fiscal simulator work?
jsonld.a8: The fiscal simulator calculates your income tax in the destination country and compares it to your current situation. It integrates special regimes, double taxation treaties and legal optimizations.
